title: Metrics Comparison MicroSim
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Drag data points or add outliers to a scatter plot and compare how MAE, MSE, RMSE, and R-squared respond to the same prediction errors.

educational.topic: Regression error metrics (MAE, MSE, RMSE, R-squared)
learningObjectives: Students will be able to compare how MAE, MSE, RMSE, and R-squared respond to the same set of prediction errors and explain why RMSE is more sensitive to outliers than MAE.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Direct manipulation of data with immediate numeric and visual feedback
keyQuestions: Why does one large residual raise RMSE by a larger factor than MAE?
RMSE is never smaller than MAE. When are the two equal?
What happens to the fitted line, and to the other residuals, when an outlier is added?
commonMisconceptions: MAE and RMSE always tell the same story (they agree when the errors are similar in size and move apart when a few errors are much larger than the rest).
Positive and negative errors cancel out in these metrics (absolute values and squares are never negative, so every miss adds to the total).
MSE is in the same units as the target (it is in squared units, and RMSE converts it back).
An outlier changes only its own residual (the least-squares line moves toward it, so the other residuals change as well).
assessmentOpportunities: Given the residuals 1, −1, 2, −2, and 10, students compute MAE, MSE, and RMSE by hand, state which metric the largest residual affects most, and justify the answer using its share of each total.
